lesson.title: Three New Letters: ਕ, ਖ, and ਗ
lesson.subject: punjabi

contentBlocks.text: You know five letters so far! Today we start a new row of the Gurmukhi alphabet with three letters that sound related to each other: ਕ (kakka), ਖ (khakha), and ਗ (gagga).

ਕ (kakka) makes a 'k' sound, like in 'kite'. ਖ (khakha) makes a breathier 'kh' sound, pushed out with more air. ਗ (gagga) makes a 'g' sound, like in 'go'. Practice saying all three in a row: ka... kha... ga. Notice they all belong to the same family of sounds, made in the same part of your mouth.
You now know eight letters! Practice saying all of them in order: ura, aira, iri, sassa, haha, kakka, khakha, gagga.

objectives: Recognize and name the letters ਕ (kakka), ਖ (khakha), and ਗ (gagga)
Notice that these three letters belong to a related sound family (all made in a similar part of the mouth)
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review all five letters learned so far — can the child name them in order?
2. Introduce ਕ, ਖ, ਗ one at a time, saying each name aloud together three times.
3. Practice the sound family together: ka... kha... ga, noticing how similar they feel to say.
4. Trace each letter in the air before picking up a pencil.
5. Move to the worksheet: trace each letter, then write it once more on the practice line.
6. Close by reciting all eight letters learned so far, in order.
differentiationTips: Struggling: focus on just ਕ and ਗ (the two more distinct sounds) before adding ਖ's subtler breathy difference
Ready for more: ask the child to guess what sound might come next in this row of the alphabet (ਘ and ਙ)
For a child who enjoys patterns, point out that Gurmukhi organizes consonants into rows of related sounds, unlike the English alphabet
teacherGuide.answerKey: This is a tracing and recognition activity — check that each traced letter roughly matches the shape shown.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: ਕ, ਖ, ਗ begin the first full consonant row of the traditional Painti Akhari sequence, continuing the systematic letter-by-letter progression from the previous two lessons.
